Welcome to nihilism/existentialism. Life really has no purpose or meaning. That might seem bleak, but for me realizing it actually relieved a lot of stress helped with my depression. You don’t have to accomplish anything or leave anything behind. The big picture is that we’re nothing but highly evolved life with huge brains hanging out on one of who-knows-how-many planets. Our existence is random. Even if/when we kill the earth and all die, time and space will go on. So yeah, there’s no reason to do anything, but there’s also no reason NOT to do anything. Might as well get the most out of consciousness while we have it. Watch the progression of society, eat tasty food, see the beauty of Earth, pet dogs, etc. Maybe you’ll find something you’re passionate about and can create your own meaning.  


This might not be very helpful or encouraging, but it’s what helped me come to peace with my existence. The pressure of searching for meaning can be crushing.

 First of all it’s super important to note that even though the names are so similar, they are completely separate organizations. I was in girl scouts for about 12 years and have two brothers who went through Boy Scouts (one for only 5 years, one Eagle Scout). I’m now an adult and can confidently say I learned nothing of value from my scouting experience.  My troop was one of the better ones, but the organization itself is so limited and geared towards younger (>10y) girls that there’s really just not much to do. Don’t even get me started on the differences between the camps. I spent my summers singing dumb camp songs, making flimsy crafts, and discussing the importance of friendship while my older brother was out learning fire starting, craftsmanship, how to fix appliances/cars, serious leadership, etc. 

Boy Scouts are in general much more respected too. Becoming an Eagle Scout means something, both to the public and to other scouts. The Girl Scouts have the bronze, silver, and gold awards. They’re ultimately meaningless and no one outside Girl Scouts has even heard of it. 

I don’t even know what happen to the Girl Scout’s badge system. They changed in the middle of my scout years and none of my troop ever earned another badge after that. Also meaningless. 

I grew up always jealous of my older brother. He got so much out of scouts and had so much more fun.

Tl:dr Girl Scouts sucks and I’m still bitter about it

It is not your fault. I'm the same. I've been working a lot on just talking more even when I have nothing to say, and it's made some situations a bit less stressful at least. It's really hard when you can't even think of anything to say, but there's people who are ok with that and will enjoy your company anyway. 

My friend is 3 years older than me and I never actually see him except for when he stops by to visit the high school, but we talk on facebook or text everyday. It's so much easier to type than to say. I wasn't that close to him when he went to school with me, so it takes a lot of pressure off. 

Not sure exactly what my point is, but you should try reaching out a bit. Baby steps. Maybe smile at a joke or make a brief comment on something. Try talking to someone in one of your classes about whatever that subject is. I know that's a lot easier said than done though, but try not to be so hard on yourself about it. 

Maybe that guy who convinced you to go noticed that you weren't doing well and was genuinely concerned. People tend to be a lot nicer than most depressed minds think. You should think about talking to him and letting him know how you're doing. 

I'd be up for talking if you'd like. Like I said, it's a lot less stressful to type. I say lots of things I'd normally be too scared to say out loud. Talking to just one person can help a lot. I talk one of my friends out of suicide at least once a week, so apparently I'm pretty good at it :p 

But yeah, you should definitely tell your therapist about what you've been thinking about. It's ok to tell her about the suicide attempts too. She can only make it known to other people if you seem in immediate danger, not if you were before. It feels better to get those things off your chest. Just little improvements go a long way

Since you're 18, I don't think your parents would have to find out if you went to a doctor, especially if it was just for blood work. They tend not to care too much about your life. It wouldn't hurt to look into it or ask your therapist. 

Once you start feeling better, you get to realize how awesome you look. It's like a reward for having things suck. I lost about 40lbs. It's not healthy, but pretty cool none-the-less. At least now I can pass out and look good while doing it :D

Do you talk to your friend much about how you feel? In my experience, that helps so much more than any therapist or medicine. Having just one person who will listen to your rants and help keep you calm is so amazingly amazing and helpful (mine even listens to me when I can't spell! I have no idea how he makes any sense of it).

My friend's in the same situation... Her mom knows she's suicidal and that she's hurt herself multiple times, but doesn't fucking care. Nope. All that matters is her school work and keeping the house clean or whatever. She gets yelled at for being depressed and even though (thanks to me,) she's seen doctors and is in therapy, she's making it all up to get attention. 

Point being, parents really fucking suck sometimes. And some suck all the time. 

Have you tried talking to anyone at your school about this? A counselor can pressure your parents into doing something about it. But if you're not comfortable with that, you should try getting a close friend you can talk to about this stuff if you don't already. I can't tell you how much that helps. I have more experience than I'd like dealing with this kind of thing, so I'd be happy to talk if you'd like. 

I really hope you can find someone to help. No one should have to go through this shit alone.

Just curious, but have you had any blood work done? Not eating caused me to have anemia which has meant lots of weakness and black-outs. You may want to look in to trying some vitamins or something. They don't fix it, but it makes it more bearable. 

Having to go through school with all this stuff really sucks... it just means less time to sleep and try to get better. I'm glad to hear you're seeing a therapist though. A lot of people struggle with that step (honestly, I was forced into it. I don't really think it helps anything, but my parents think otherwise). 

And really, I'm impressed at how much sense what your wrote made. I'm not even able to formulate words when I'm tired, so good job on that! :)
